source_indices.finding: 223 cells represent lunar months; glyphs mark possible eclipses, and about a third of the scale survives. Missing portions involve reconstruction. Letter forms under discussion occur from late third to mid-first century BCE and do not narrow construction within that range.
The 223-synodic-month cycle was used in Late Babylonian eclipse prediction; the authors distinguish inferred date of adoption from dates of observations compiled retrospectively.
The abstract gives approximately the end of the second century BCE; the body infers 150–100 BCE from lettering, distinct from the later wreck date.
